title: Legislative districts of Caloocan

{{Short description|Legislative districts in the Philippines' House of Representatives}} {{Politics of the Philippines}} The '''legislative districts of Caloocan''' are the representations of the [[Cities of the Philippines#Independent cities|highly urbanized city]] of [[Caloocan]] in the [[List of legislatures of the Philippines|various national legislatures]] of the [[Philippines]]. The city is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the [[Congress of the Philippines]] through its [[Caloocan's 1st congressional district|first]], [[Caloocan's 2nd congressional district|second]], and [[Caloocan's 3rd congressional district|third]] congressional districts. == History == {{further|Legislative districts of Rizal|Legislative districts of Manila|Legislative districts of Quezon City}} Caloocan was initially represented as part of the [[Manila's at-large congressional district|at-large district]] of the [[Manila (province)|province of Manila]] in the [[Malolos Congress]] from 1898 to 1899. The then-town was later incorporated to the province of [[Rizal (province)|Rizal]], established in 1901, and was represented as part of the [[Rizal's 1st congressional district|first district]] of Rizal from 1907 to 1941 and from 1945 to 1972. In the disruption caused by the [[World War II]], it was incorporated to the [[City of Greater Manila]]{{cite PH act|chamber=EO|number=400, s. 1942|title=Creating the City of Greater Manila|date=January 1, 1942|accessdate=August 24, 2022|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/1942/01/01/executive-order-no-400-s-1942/}} and was represented as part of the at-large district of Manila in the [[National Assembly (Second Philippine Republic)|National Assembly of the Second Philippine Republic]] from 1943 to 1944. Caloocan was separated from Rizal on November 7, 1975 by virtue of Presidential Decree No. 824 signed by President [[Ferdinand Marcos]],{{cite PH act|url=http://www.lawphil.net/statutes/presdecs/pd1975/pd_824_1975.html|chamber=PD|number=824|date=November 7, 1975|access-date=October 10, 2017|title=Creating the Metropolitan Manila and the Metropolitan Manila Commission and for Other Purposes}} and was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] along with other [[Metro Manila|Metropolitan Manila]] municipalities and cities as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region IV]] from 1978 to 1984. Caloocan first gained separate representation in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]], when it elected [[#At-large (defunct)|two assemblymen]] at-large to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] from 1984 to 1986. It was later divided into two districts upon the restoration of the House of Representatives in 1987. Of the country’s 238 legislative districts, the first legislative district of Caloocan was the biggest in terms of population size, with 1.19 million persons as of 2015.{{cite web|url=https://www.psa.gov.ph/content/population-counts-legislative-district-based-2015-census-population|title=Population Counts by Legislative District (Based on the 2015 Census of Population)|website=Philippine Statistics Authority|access-date=December 6, 2016}} In 2021, the [[Senate of the Philippines|Senate]] passed on third and final reading House Bill No. 7700, a bill creating the third legislative district of Caloocan. It divided the first district into two legislative districts. The first legislative district would be composed of Barangays 1 to 4, Barangays 77 to 85 and Barangays 132 to 177 while Barangays 178 to 188 would form the third legislative district.{{cite web | url = https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1404989/senate-passes-bills-creating-new-caloocan-bulacan-legislative-districts | title = Senate passes bills creating new Caloocan, Bulacan legislative districts | website = INQUIRER.net | date = 9 March 2021 | accessdate = 11 April 2021 }} It was later approved by President [[Rodrigo Duterte]] on May 26, 2021 as he signed this law under Republic Act No. 11545.{{cite PH act |title=An Act Reapportioning the First Legislative District of the City of Caloocan into Two (2) Legislative Districts |chamber=RA |number=11545 |folio= |language= |date=May 26, 2021 |year= |article= |section= |url=https://www.lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2021/ra_11545_2021.html |accessdate=April 10, 2022 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20220410022951/https://www.lawphil.net/statutes/repacts/ra2021/ra_11545_2021.html |archivedate=April 10, 2022 |url-status=dead |ref= }}{{cite web|url=https://www.pna.gov.ph/articles/1141650|title=Legislative districts in Caloocan, Bulacan reapportioned|website=Philippine News Agency|access-date=May 27, 2021}} == Current districts == {| class="wikitable sortable" style="margin: 1em auto; font-size:100%; line-height:20px; text-align:center" |+Legislative Districts and Congressional Representatives of [[Caloocan]] |- !District ! colspan="3" |Current Representative !Party !
